_README: Vietnam fact layer. CONTAINS ONLY PRIMARY-VERIFIED FACTS — every row's source_url was opened and read on checked_at. Anything provisional, consensus-only or secondary deliberately did NOT make it in; it stays in raw/claude.json under _open_questions and in disputes.md. An absent fact means 'not proven', never 'not true'. serve_live values (exchange rates, prices, daily budgets, AQI) are intentionally absent and must be served live, never frozen here.

_meta.built_from: raw/claude.json + raw/chatgpt.json + raw/deepseek.json, reconciled; promoted by hand | 2026-10-17 Stage 0b wishlist pass: P1 rows verified directly against primary/official sources (read this session), no external-model panel

timezone.value: Vietnam has a single time zone (Indochina Time, UTC+7) and does not observe daylight saving, so the gap to the United States shifts by an hour twice a year. It is 12 hours ahead of Washington DC during Eastern Standard Time and 11 hours ahead during Eastern Daylight Time.
timezone.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
timezone.support: State Dept Vietnam page states Vietnam has one time zone and does not observe daylight saving. CORRECTED 2026-10-12: that page also states Vietnam is '11 hours ahead of Washington, D.C. during Eastern Standard Time', which is arithmetically wrong — UTC+7 against UTC-5 is 12 hours, and 11 hours applies to EDT (UTC-4). The figures here are the computed ones. A PRIMARY SOURCE CAN BE WRONG ON A COMPUTABLE FACT; check the arithmetic rather than copying the number.

type.value: A visa is required. There is no general visa exemption for US passport holders; the e-visa is the normal route. The main exception is a stay of 30 days or less on the island of Phu Quoc, arriving and leaving directly. A separate narrow exception exists for overseas Vietnamese holding a 5-year visa-exemption certificate.
type.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
type.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'A visa is required. You must apply for a visa before you travel. An exception is allowed for stays of 30 days or less on the island of Phu Quoc only.'

max_stay_days.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
max_stay_days.support: Vietnam Immigration Department e-visa FAQ, citing the Law on Entry, Exit, Transit and Residence of Foreigners 2014 (amended 2019, 2023): 'the visa cannot exceed 90 days'. Corroborated by the US Embassy ('up to 90 days').

fee.value: USD 25 for a single-entry e-visa, USD 50 for multiple entry, payable by bank transfer.
fee.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
fee.support: US Embassy Hanoi, verbatim: 'E-visas are issued with a validity period of up to 90 days, one-entry for 25 USD or multiple entries for 50 USD, and payable via bank transfer.' evisa.gov.vn publishes no public fee schedule.

processing_time.value: Usually 3 to 5 working days after the Immigration Department receives the completed application and payment; longer during application surges or holidays.
processing_time.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
processing_time.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'E-visa applications are usually processed within 3 to 5 working days after the Vietnam Immigration Department receives the completed application and payment. However, this time may change depending on the number of applications or holidays.' Counter-evidence exists (Vietnam's embassy in India publishes 05-30 working days), so do not promise the lower figure.

passport_validity_vs_evisa.value: An e-visa's validity must be at least 30 days shorter than the passport's remaining validity. This never binds an eligible tourist: a 90-day e-visa needs roughly four months of passport validity, and Vietnam already requires six months at entry, so anyone who can enter already satisfies it.
passport_validity_vs_evisa.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
passport_validity_vs_evisa.support: evisa.gov.vn FAQ, verbatim: 'the validity of the electronic visa must be at least 30 days shorter than the passport validity.' The second sentence is arithmetic on that rule (90 + 30 = 120 days), not a sourced claim. CORRECTED 2026-10-12: an earlier version asserted that a passport expiring in just over six months could not carry a 90-day visa. That was my own inference and it was wrong — the second gate caught it. A 'verified' status covers the SOURCE's claim only; never append your own reasoning inside a verified value.

pre_arrival_declaration.value: A pre-arrival declaration is filed online at prearrival.immigration.gov.vn. It is free, takes about ten minutes, is separate from the visa, and is filed no earlier than three days before arrival. Note the two governments describe its status differently: the US State Department says travellers on a non-Vietnamese passport arriving by air must complete it, while Vietnam's own Immigration Department portal presents it as advisory, saying only that submitting in advance helps reduce waiting time at immigration.
pre_arrival_declaration.scope: Non-Vietnamese passport holders arriving in Vietnam by air
pre_arrival_declaration.support: Portal confirmed official: title 'Pre-Arrival Information - Cuc Quan ly xuat nhap canh' on an immigration.gov.vn domain, text 'Submitting your declaration in advance helps reduce waiting time at the immigration area.' The mandatory framing and the three-day window are from travel.state.gov: 'All travelers on a non-Vietnamese passport and entering Vietnam by air must also fill out a pre-arrival declaration form no earlier than 3 days prior to their arrival.' The discrepancy between the two is deliberately preserved in the value.

entry_gates.value: An e-visa is valid at 83 designated international border gates — 17 airports, 27 land crossings and 39 seaports — since Resolution 389/NQ-CP of 2 December 2025 added 41 to the previous 42. Every international airport an American would fly into is covered. Gate eligibility is a separate question from the port you select on your application, which is binding.
entry_gates.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
entry_gates.support: Vietnam Government Portal (baochinhphu.vn), 3 Dec 2025: Resolution No. 389/NQ-CP dated December 2, 2025 brings the total ports to 83. Corroborated by Vietnam Law Magazine, VietnamPlus and the National Tourism Administration (17 airports / 27 land / 39 seaports). SUPERSEDES the figure of 42 still published by vn.usembassy.gov as of 2026-10-12 — a US primary source lagging a Vietnamese regulatory change by ten months. Long Thanh airport appears in some lists but is not yet operational; do not write it as usable.

no_extension_in_country.value: An e-visa cannot be renewed or extended from inside Vietnam, and Vietnam usually grants only the period requested rather than the maximum. Changing the duration means leaving and applying again from outside, not filing anything locally.
no_extension_in_country.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
no_extension_in_country.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'Vietnam does not allow you to renew or extend an E-visa while you are in the country.' and 'Vietnam usually only gives you a visa for the exact time period you requested.' CORRECTED 2026-10-12: an earlier version said 'the duration decision is made at application and cannot be corrected later'. The source establishes an IN-COUNTRY limitation only; a fresh application from outside Vietnam is available, so the broader finality claim was unsupported and inflated the handoff.

port_must_match.value: The entry and exit location on an e-visa must match the port chosen in the application. An e-visa naming one airport does not work at another, and an error on the e-visa can mean refused entry.
port_must_match.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
port_must_match.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'The entry and exit location must match the port of entry you chose when you applied.' and 'If your E-visa has an error, immigration may not let you enter the country. You may have to pay a travel agency at the airport for an expensive visa sponsorship.'

must_print.value: The e-visa must be printed and carried with the passport at entry.
must_print.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
must_print.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'You must print your E-visa and bring it with your valid passport when you enter Vietnam.'

exemption_excludes_us.value: US passport holders are not covered by Vietnam's unilateral visa-exemption scheme and must hold a visa. The 45-day exemption extended to 12 further European countries by Resolution 229/NQ-CP runs 15 August 2025 to 14 August 2028 and does not include the United States, Canada or Australia. The one exception for Americans is the Vietnamese diaspora: an overseas Vietnamese with the relevant documents can hold a 5-year visa-exemption certificate.
exemption_excludes_us.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
exemption_excludes_us.support: travel.state.gov states a visa is required for US passports. Resolution 229/NQ-CP was issued 8 August 2025, effective 15 August 2025 to 14 August 2028 — confirmed by Vietnam's own embassies (Japan, Switzerland) and LuatVietnam. CORRECTED 2026-10-12: an earlier version dated this expansion to 2026.

phu_quoc_exception.value: A stay of 30 days or less on the island of Phu Quoc is exempt from the visa requirement, provided you do not clear immigration on the mainland.
phu_quoc_exception.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
phu_quoc_exception.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'An exception is allowed for stays of 30 days or less on the island of Phu Quoc only.'

passport_validity.value: The passport must be valid at entry with six months' validity beyond the arrival date, and carry blank pages for stamps. Allow at least two blank pages.
passport_validity.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
passport_validity.support: State Dept states 'Your passport must have 6 months validity beyond your arrival date.' NOTE: the same page contradicts itself on blank pages, saying both 'You must have 1 blank page available per stamp' and 'Your passport must have at least 2 blank pages required for stamps.' The conservative figure is recorded here deliberately.

emergency_passport.value: Vietnam may not accept the 12-page US emergency passport for e-visa entry, so a passport replaced mid-trip at a US embassy in the region may not get you in.
emergency_passport.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
emergency_passport.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'Vietnam may not accept the 12-page U.S. emergency passport for e-visa for entry.'

currency_declaration.value: There is no limit on currency brought in or out, but a declaration is required above either threshold: more than 15,000,000 VND, or more than 5,000 USD in foreign currency.
currency_declaration.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
currency_declaration.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'Entry maximum: None. However, you must declare any Vietnamese Dong over 15,000,000 VND or any foreign currency over 5,000 USD.' The same thresholds are stated for exit. A competing figure of USD 7,000 circulates and traces to a superseded 2005 embassy notice.

police_registration.value: Every visitor must have their overnight address registered with the local police, Vietnamese citizens included. Hotels do this automatically at check-in, which is why they take your passport. In informal stays such as an Airbnb or a homestay the host is responsible, and it is worth confirming they have done it.
police_registration.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
police_registration.support: US Embassy Hanoi, verbatim: 'all visitors (including Vietnamese) are required to register their temporary residence with the police station where they are staying overnight.' No official statement of the consequence for a short-stay tourist was found, so none is asserted.

exit_control.value: Leaving Vietnam requires a valid visa, a residence card, or Immigration Department approval. The State Department warns that if you cannot leave on time for any reason, including a medical emergency, you will likely pay overstay fines and face delays getting permission to leave.
exit_control.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
exit_control.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'Vietnam requires a valid visa, residence card, or approval from the Immigration Department to leave the country.' and 'If you change your plans or cannot leave Vietnam on time for any reason, including a medical emergency, you will likely pay overstay fines and face delays getting permission to leave.' CORRECTED 2026-10-12: an earlier version rendered 'you will likely pay' as 'overstaying brings fines and delays', dropping the qualifier, and treated an expired visa as an absolute departure bar when the source lists Immigration Department approval as an alternative route out.

child_exit.value: A US-citizen child of Vietnamese parentage may need a Vietnamese passport or a Vietnamese exit visa to leave Vietnam. The requirement attaches to parentage, not to how the child entered.
child_exit.support: US Embassy Hanoi: 'In general, a Vietnamese passport or a Vietnamese exit visa is required by the Vietnamese government in the event your child needs to exit Vietnam.'

hotel_registration_law.value: By law it is the hotel, homestay or host who must declare a foreign guest's temporary residence to the local police, within 12 hours of arrival (24 hours in remote areas), usually electronically. The statute does not require you to surrender your passport; the desk needs its details to file the declaration, so handing it over for copying and asking for it back is consistent with the law. Many hotels still hold it during the stay as a deposit practice, and may ask for prepayment if you insist on keeping it.
hotel_registration_law.scope: Foreign guests at any accommodation in Vietnam
hotel_registration_law.support: Law No. 47/2014/QH13 on Entry, Exit, Transit and Residence of Foreigners (English text, LuatVietnam), Article 33: foreigners temporarily residing in Vietnam declare 'via managers and executives of accommodation establishments' to the commune/ward police; clause 2: declarations filed 'within 12 hours or within 24 hours, for remote and deep-lying areas, after the foreigners arrive'; no passport-surrender provision. US Embassy Hanoi (vietnamese-visas-and-entry-exit, read 2026-10-17): 'all visitors (including Vietnamese) are required to register their temporary residence with the police station where they are staying overnight.' Corrections #7 governs: state no consequence. The hold-as-deposit practice is guidebook observation (Moon 2015 p497), not law.

advisory_level.value: Level 1 - Exercise Normal Precautions, the lowest of the State Department's four levels. Date issued: June 24, 2026.
advisory_level.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
advisory_level.support: State Dept Vietnam travel advisory header: 'Level 1 - Exercise normal precautions', 'Date issued: June 24, 2026'.

main_risk.value: Vietnam is generally safe for travellers; petty crime is the common risk, especially in tourist areas, with bag and phone snatching from moving motorbikes the dominant mode. Violent crime against foreigners is rare. Road traffic is the hazard the State Department warns about at greatest length, and the one most likely to put a visitor in hospital.
main_risk.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
main_risk.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'Vietnam is generally a safe destination for travelers. Petty crime is common, especially in popular tourist locations.' CORRECTED 2026-10-12: an earlier version asserted road traffic was 'the leading cause of serious injury to visitors', a statistical ranking the source does not make — it gives extensive road-safety and licence warnings, which supports emphasis, not a ranking. The second gate caught the fact layer's own support not matching its claim.

uxo.value: Unexploded ordnance remains a real but narrowly located hazard. Risk is concentrated at construction sites and is low in urban and populated areas, including tourist destinations.
uxo.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
uxo.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'Areas of greatest risk are construction sites. Landmine risk is low in urban and populated areas, including tourist destinations.'

vaccines_required.value: No vaccinations are required to enter Vietnam. This is an entry requirement only and is not medical advice; several vaccines are recommended without being required.
vaccines_required.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
vaccines_required.support: State Dept Vietnam entry requirements, verbatim: 'No vaccinations are required.'

vaccines_recommended.value: CDC recommends for Vietnam: Hepatitis A for unvaccinated travellers aged one and over, Hepatitis B for unvaccinated travellers of all ages, and Typhoid for most travellers, alongside routine vaccines and COVID-19. Japanese encephalitis, rabies and monkeypox are conditional on length of stay, rural exposure or specific activities rather than recommended for every traveller.
vaccines_recommended.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
vaccines_recommended.support: CDC Travelers' Health Vietnam destination page, Vaccines and Medicines table: Hepatitis A 'Recommended for unvaccinated travelers one year old or older going to Vietnam'; Hepatitis B 'Recommended for unvaccinated travelers of all ages'; Typhoid 'Recommended for most travelers'; Japanese Encephalitis recommended for those moving to or spending long periods in affected areas.

malaria.value: Malaria transmission in Vietnam is rural only, with rare cases in the Mekong and Red River deltas, and CDC lists no transmission in the cities of Da Nang, Hai Phong, Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Nha Trang or Quy Nhon. For the deltas CDC recommends no chemoprophylaxis, only bite precautions. Chloroquine and mefloquine resistance is present in ten named provinces (Binh Duong, Binh Phuoc, Dak Lak, Dak Nong, Gia Lai, Khanh Hoa, Kon Tum, Lam Dong, Ninh Thuan, Tay Ninh), where CDC points to atovaquone-proguanil, doxycycline or tafenoquine; in other transmission areas mefloquine is also listed. Whether any prophylaxis is warranted depends on the specific rural areas visited.
malaria.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
malaria.support: CDC Vietnam destination page, malaria section 'Updated April 23, 2025', page reviewed August 25, 2026, re-read 2026-10-17: 'Rural areas only; rare cases in the Mekong and Red River Deltas'; 'None in the cities of Da Nang, Hai Phong, Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon), Nha Trang, and Quy Nhon'; deltas: 'No chemoprophylaxis recommended (insect bite precautions and mosquito avoidance only)'; provinces listed for atovaquone-proguanil, doxycycline, tafenoquine: Binh Duong, Binh Phuoc, Dak Lak, Dak Nong, Gia Lai, Khanh Hoa, Kon Tum, Lam Dong, Ninh Thuan, Tay Ninh; resistance 'Chloroquine and mefloquine'. Three 2015–16 guidebooks give three different readings; this page is the only authority.

drug_laws.value: Drug offences carry severe penalties and police sometimes test blood for drugs. Substances consumed legally in another country before arrival can still be detected and lead to arrest and a long prison sentence. Ingredients in some common prescription medicines, including for ADHD, may be illegal in Vietnam.
drug_laws.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
drug_laws.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'Using narcotic drugs in Vietnam is illegal. Police sometimes test people's blood for drugs. If drugs are in your system, even if you used them in another country where they were legal, you can be arrested and face a long prison sentence. Please note that some ingredients for common prescription drugs to treat conditions such as ADHD may be illegal in Vietnam.'

consular_access.value: Consular access to detained US citizens is routinely delayed, often by several weeks, so the US Embassy may not be able to reach you quickly if something goes wrong.
consular_access.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
consular_access.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'Vietnamese authorities routinely delay notification and consular access to detained U.S. citizens, often leading to delays of several weeks or more for embassy visits.'

emergency_numbers.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
emergency_numbers.support: State Dept transportation section, verbatim: 'Dial 113 for traffic police', 'Dial 115 for ambulance services', 'Dial 1900-54-55-70 for Vietnam Expressway Corporation (VEC hotline)'. The fire number is deliberately omitted: it was not stated on any primary source opened.

air_quality.value: Air pollution is a significant problem in Vietnam's major cities, Hanoi above all, and travellers with respiratory conditions should consult a doctor before travelling. Current readings are volatile and must be checked live rather than quoted.
air_quality.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
air_quality.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'Air pollution is a significant problem in Vietnam's major cities, especially Hanoi. You should consult your doctor prior to travel and consider the impact that poor air quality may have on you.'

driving_licence.value: A US driver's licence and an International Driving Permit are both invalid in Vietnam. Driving without a Vietnamese licence can mean a fine, arrest or jail, renting a moped or motorbike without one is illegal, and travel insurance may not pay medical bills after an accident without a licence. Licence conversion requires residency documentation a short-stay visitor does not hold.
driving_licence.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
driving_licence.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'U.S. driver's licenses and International Driving Permits do not work in Vietnam. If you drive without a Vietnamese license, you can be fined, arrested, or sent to jail.' and 'Renting a moped or motorbike without a Vietnamese driver's license is illegal. If you get in an accident without a license, your travel insurance may not pay your medical bills.' The conversion-requires-residency half is secondary and is stated here only as the reason no short-trip route exists; the licence invalidity and its consequences are primary.

traffic_laws.value: Vietnamese law requires helmets, speed-limit compliance and zero alcohol while driving — zero, not a blood-alcohol threshold. Enforcement is tightening, with higher fines and cameras in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. Licence, vehicle registration and identification must be carried while driving.
traffic_laws.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
traffic_laws.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'Although laws require helmets, following speed limits, and zero alcohol while driving, many people don't follow these rules consistently. The government is cracking down with higher fines and cameras in big cities like Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City.' Required documents listed as valid driver's license, vehicle registration, personal identification.

driving_penalty.value: Driving without a Vietnamese licence can result in a fine, arrest, or jail.
driving_penalty.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'If you drive without a Vietnamese license, you can be fined, arrested, or sent to jail.'

unlicensed_insurance.value: After an accident while riding without a valid licence, travel insurance may not pay your medical bills.
unlicensed_insurance.scope: US ordinary passport holders travelling to Vietnam as tourists
unlicensed_insurance.support: State Dept, verbatim: 'If you get in an accident without a license, your travel insurance may not pay your medical bills.'

red_light_no_turn.value: A red light means stop, and there is no general right turn on red in Vietnam. A right turn on red is lawful only where a supplementary right-turn arrow signal or sign permits it. Two 2015–16 guidebooks said the opposite (one claimed right on red was allowed everywhere except Hanoi); the 2024 law settles it.
red_light_no_turn.scope: Anyone driving or riding in Vietnam; also relevant to pedestrians judging traffic
red_light_no_turn.support: Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety No. 36/2024/QH15 (in force 1 Jan 2025), Article 11 clause 4(c): 'The red light signal means stop.' Tuoi Tre News explainer of 20 Jan 2025 on the same law: drivers cannot turn in any direction on a red signal; where a designated right-turn arrow is lit, a right turn on red is not a violation. Decree 168/2024 sets the fines.

helmets_all_riders.value: Every rider and every passenger on a motorbike, moped or motorised bicycle must wear a helmet meeting the national technical standard, with the chin strap fastened. This covers pillion passengers on motorbike taxis. A xe om driver's spare helmet satisfies the letter of the law but little else, so bring or buy a proper one for any real riding.
helmets_all_riders.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
helmets_all_riders.support: Law 36/2024/QH15 Article 33 clause 2: drivers and passengers of two- or three-wheeled motorcycles and mopeds 'shall wear crash helmets up to national technical regulations' with chin straps fastened correctly; Article 31 clause 3 applies the same to motorised bicycles. Passenger fines under Decree 168/2024 are reported by Vietnamese legal press and are not printed here.

no_licence_prohibited_act.value: Operating a motor vehicle without the driving licence the law requires is itself a listed prohibited act under the 2024 traffic law, and letting an unqualified person drive is a second one. This is the Vietnamese statute behind the State Department's warning, and it is why every car hire comes with a driver.
no_licence_prohibited_act.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
no_licence_prohibited_act.support: Law 36/2024/QH15 Article 9 clause 1 lists among prohibited acts operating motor vehicles without a driver's licence 'as required by law'; Article 9 clause 7 prohibits 'Letting unqualified persons operate motor vehicles or special-purpose vehicles on the road'. Corroborates facts.json transport.driving_licence (State Dept) and corrections #2.
no_licence_prohibited_act.note: Article 55 (foreign-plated vehicles) sits behind the publisher's paywall and was not read.

ride_hailing_legal.value: App-based ride-hailing (Grab and similar) has operated nationwide as a regular licensed business since 1 April 2020 under Decree 10/2020/ND-CP, which ended the earlier pilot limited to a few provinces. Ride-hailing cars must carry a reflective 'contract car' sign on the front and rear windscreens, which is how to tell a legitimate app car from a freelancer.
ride_hailing_legal.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
ride_hailing_legal.support: Vietnam Investment Review (24 Feb 2020): Decree 10/2020/ND-CP replaces Decree 86/2014/ND-CP; 'Grab and other ride-hailing firms can officially operate nationwide from April 1, 2020'; contract-based vehicles must affix a 'Contract Car' sign of reflective material, minimum 06 x 20 cm, on front and rear windshields. Corroborated by Baker McKenzie client alert (13 Mar 2020) and KrASIA.

metro_hanoi.value: Hanoi has two operating metro lines run by Hanoi Metro: Line 2A (Cat Linh to Ha Dong, 12 stations) and Line 3 (Nhon to Hanoi Station), of which only the elevated western section is open. Both run 05:30 to 22:00. Neither line serves the airport or the Old Quarter directly; Cat Linh is the closest Line 2A station to the centre.
metro_hanoi.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
metro_hanoi.support: Operator site metrohanoi.vn (Cong ty TNHH MTV Duong sat Ha Noi / Hanoi Metro), read 2026-10-17: 'Tuyen 2A: Cat Linh - Ha Dong' 12 stations; 'Tuyen 3: Nhon - Ga Ha Noi' 12 stations; operating hours '05:30 - 22:00' for both; notice 2507-TB-DSHN dated 11.9.2026. Line 3 underground section (Kim Ma to Hanoi Station) still under construction with a late-2027 target per VTV/VietnamPlus and Tuoi Tre; the elevated section opened 8 Aug 2024 (Tuoi Tre, 9 Aug 2025).
metro_hanoi.note: Fares not printed: the operator's ticket page was not readable.

metro_hcmc_line1.value: Ho Chi Minh City Metro Line 1 (Ben Thanh to Suoi Tien, 19.7 km, 14 stations) opened 22 December 2024 and is run by HURC1. It runs from 05:00 to 22:00 on weekdays and to 23:00 on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays, every 6 to 8 minutes at peak and 10 to 12 minutes off-peak. Ben Thanh is the District 1 terminus; the line does not reach the airport.
metro_hcmc_line1.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
metro_hcmc_line1.support: Tuoi Tre News, 17 Aug 2025: operator 'Ho Chi Minh City Urban Railway No. 1 Company Limited'; service from 05:00 daily, to 22:00 weekdays and 23:00 Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays; peak headway 6–8 minutes, off-peak 10–12; 243 weekday / 246 weekend trips from September 2025. Opening date 22 Dec 2024 per Tuoi Tre (Dec 2024) and VTV (Jan 2025).

metro_hcmc_fares.value: HCMC Metro Line 1 fares set by the city People's Committee: single trips 7,000 to 20,000 VND cash by distance, or 6,000 to 19,000 VND cashless; a one-day pass 40,000 VND; a three-day pass 90,000 VND; a monthly pass 300,000 VND. In US terms the longest ride is under a dollar.
metro_hcmc_fares.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
metro_hcmc_fares.support: VnEconomy, 23 Nov 2024, reporting the HCMC People's Committee fare decision: cash 7,000–20,000 VND per trip; cashless 6,000–19,000; day pass 40,000 (unlimited); 3-day pass 90,000; monthly 300,000 (students 150,000). Vietnam News (Nov 2024) reports the same figures. Fares are official tariffs, not estimates; re-check after any fare revision.

airport_bus_hcmc_109.value: Public bus 109 links the Saigon bus station next to Ben Thanh Market with Tan Son Nhat airport, and since 28 April 2025 it serves the new Terminal 3 (domestic) instead of Terminals 1 and 2. It runs roughly 05:30 to 22:40 from the airport and 05:45 to 22:30 from the city, with fares between 8,000 and 15,000 VND. International arrivals land at Terminal 2, so check which bus currently serves T2 before relying on 109.
airport_bus_hcmc_109.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
airport_bus_hcmc_109.support: VOH (Voice of Ho Chi Minh City), 28 Apr 2025, reporting the HCMC Public Transport Management Center announcement: route 109 'ket noi truc tiep voi nha ga T3 thay vi nha ga T1 va T2 nhu truoc day'; hours 05:30–22:40 at T3 and 05:45–22:30 at the Saigon bus station; fare 8,000–15,000 VND per trip.
airport_bus_hcmc_109.note: Which route serves Terminal 2 after this change was not verified; treat as open.

airport_bus_hanoi_86.value: Express bus 86, run by Transerco, links Hanoi railway station on Le Duan with both Noi Bai terminals in about 55 minutes with eight stops, from early morning to late evening. It replaced the Vietnam Airlines minibus that older guidebooks describe. The fare has risen since the 2016 launch and is not printed here.
airport_bus_hanoi_86.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
airport_bus_hanoi_86.support: Viet Nam News, 30 Apr 2016: route 86 operated by 'The Ha Noi Transport Corporation (Transerco)', starting 'from the Ha Noi Station at Le Duan Street', eight stops, 33 km, departures 05:05–21:40 from the station and 06:18–22:58 from the airport, launch fare VND 30,000. Current fare conflicts across 2024–26 travel sites (30,000 vs 45,000) and no Transerco page was found, so no figure is published.

grab_pickup_sgn.value: At Tan Son Nhat, Grab's designated pickup point for international arrivals is in the parking-lot area outside the terminal, not at the kerb; follow the in-app directions to the pin and meet the driver there. Fares are fixed up front in the app, so there is nothing to negotiate, and ride-hailing is the standard answer to the airport-taxi scams the guidebooks describe.
grab_pickup_sgn.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
grab_pickup_sgn.support: Grab airport page for Tan Son Nhat, read 2026-10-17: pickup point 'International Arrival - Parking Lot Area - Tan Son Nhat International Airport'; 'Follow the in-app directions to meet your driver at the pick up location'; 'Skip the bargaining and avoid airport touts with upfront fixed fares'; advance booking offered for airport transfers.

grab_pickup_han.value: At Noi Bai, Grab's pickup points for international arrivals are at pillars 8 and 11 outside the international terminal, with a separate GrabBike point at the international terminal; follow the in-app pin. Fares are fixed before booking.
grab_pickup_han.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
grab_pickup_han.support: Grab airport page for Noi Bai, read 2026-10-17: 'International Arrival Terminal - Pillar 8 - Noi Bai International Airport', 'International Arrival Terminal - Pillar 11', 'GrabBike Pickup/Drop-off Point - International Terminal'; in-app directions; upfront fixed fares except GrabTaxi.

rail_hanoi_hcmc.value: The Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City train takes about 33 to 34 hours end to end (SE1 about 33 h, SE3 about 34 h), with daily departures. Classes are air-conditioned soft seat, six-berth hard sleeper and four-berth soft sleeper, plus a few two-berth VIP compartments on SE1/SE2. Upper berths are cheaper than lower. Booking opens about 60 days ahead, sometimes over 90 for the full route; dsvn.vn is reported to accept overseas cards but may need a Vietnamese phone number, with Baolau or 12Go as the fallback.
rail_hanoi_hcmc.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
rail_hanoi_hcmc.support: The Man in Seat 61, Vietnam page last updated 10 June 2026: SE1 Hanoi 20:50 to Saigon 05:45 two days later (~33 h); SE3 19:20 to 05:15 (~34 h); classes listed; 'Upper berths are cheaper'; booking 'opens 60 days before departure, and sometimes over 90 days'; overseas cards on dsvn.vn 'should now' be accepted. Vietnam Railways' own site (dsvn.vn) is a JavaScript app and could not be read directly.
rail_hanoi_hcmc.note: Moon 2015 and LP 2016 gave 31–36 h; the range still holds.

tet_trains.value: Trains do not stop running over Tet. For Tet 2026 Vietnam Railways ran 906 passenger trains across a plan period of 3 February to 8 March, and added short-distance services during the official holiday week rather than cutting them. The constraint is seats, not schedules: southern-route tickets for the peak days before and after Tet sold out weeks ahead. A 2016 guidebook's claim of a nine-day train blackout no longer describes reality.
tet_trains.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
tet_trains.support: Viet Nam News, 23 Jan 2026: 'Viet Nam's railway sector will operate 906 passenger trains during the upcoming Lunar New Year (Tet) holiday in 2026'; plan 'from February 3 to March 8'; 'during the official Lunar New Year holiday, from February 14 to 22, additional short-distance trains will be arranged'; southern-route peak tickets 'from February 7 to 14' sold out. Only a handful of Hanoi–Hai Phong local trains were suspended on New Year's Eve and Day 1 (Bao Hai Phong).

hanoi_halong_drive.value: Hanoi to Ha Long city by road is about 2.5 hours since the Ha Long–Hai Phong expressway and Bach Dang bridge opened on 1 September 2018, cutting the distance from 180 km to 130 km. Guidebooks printed before 2019 still say four hours.
hanoi_halong_drive.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
hanoi_halong_drive.support: Hanoi Times, Sept 2018: expressway 'shortens the time to travel from Hanoi to Ha Long from 3.5 hours to 2.5 hours'; Bizhub/Viet Nam News: cuts Hanoi–Ha Long from 180 km to 130 km, opened 1 Sept 2018. VTV quoted a government projection of 1.5 hours; the 2.5-hour figure is the conservative one. Vietnam News Agency (3 Feb 2019): the Ha Long–Van Don extension put Hanoi–Van Don at 2.5 hours 'from four'.

halong_boat_suspensions.value: Ha Long Bay cruises are grounded by the provincial waterways port authority whenever a storm or dangerous weather is forecast: it stops issuing departure permits to every tourist vessel, day boats and overnight cruises alike, until conditions clear. Operators then cancel or reschedule. Typhoon season on this coast runs roughly July to November, and winter fog and northeast monsoon winds can also hold boats in port.
halong_boat_suspensions.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
halong_boat_suspensions.support: VOH, 20 Jul 2025: 'Cang vu Duong thuy noi dia va Dang kiem phuong tien thuy tinh Quang Ninh' issued an urgent dispatch halting departure permits for all tourist passenger vessels on Ha Long Bay and inter-island routes ahead of Storm No. 3. Earlier Bao Van Hoa reports document the same mechanism for other storms and for bad weather at Bai Chay. The seasonal framing (typhoon Jul–Nov; winter fog) is from the climate layer (facts.json climate regimes via geo.ts), not this source.

us_nonstop_routes.value: The only nonstop service between the United States and Vietnam is Vietnam Airlines' San Francisco to Ho Chi Minh City flight (VN99 westbound, VN98 eastbound), four times a week on an Airbus A350-900, about 16 hours westbound and under 14 hours eastbound, with schedules published through at least late 2026. Every other routing connects in Northeast Asia. Vietnam Airlines sells Los Angeles fares, but no nonstop LAX service was confirmed.
us_nonstop_routes.scope: Travellers between the United States and Vietnam
us_nonstop_routes.support: Flightmapper SFO–SGN route page, read 2026-10-17: Vietnam Airlines VN 99, Airbus A350-900, 4 weekly (Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun), 16:30 block, schedule entries valid through 2026-10-22 and 'Effective from 2026-10-24'. Launch 29 Nov 2021 per Hanoi Times. Vietnam Airlines' own LAX page lists SGN–LAX and HAN–LAX fares without a routing description, so nonstop LAX is unverified.

international_airports.value: Vietnam has eleven airports handling scheduled international flights: Noi Bai (HAN, Hanoi), Tan Son Nhat (SGN, Ho Chi Minh City), Da Nang (DAD), Cam Ranh (CXR, for Nha Trang), Phu Quoc (PQC), Phu Bai (HUI, Hue), Van Don (VDO, Quang Ninh), Cat Bi (HPH, Hai Phong), Can Tho (VCA), Vinh (VII) and Phu Cat (UIH, Quy Nhon). Lien Khuong (DLI, Da Lat) is designated international but mainly domestic, and Long Thanh near HCMC is under construction. For an American itinerary the practical gateways remain HAN, SGN and DAD, with CXR and PQC useful for regional connections.
international_airports.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
international_airports.support: Vietjet Air travel guide 'List of Domestic and International Airports in Vietnam', read 2026-10-17: '12 international airports' listed as HAN, SGN, PQC, DAD, CXR, HUI, VDO, VCA, VII, UIH, HPH plus Lien Khuong '(proposed)' and Long Thanh '(under construction)'. No CAAV list was found; the government master plan (baochinhphu, 2023) targets 14 international airports by 2030.
international_airports.note: Airline page, not a CAAV register; the count moves as designations change.

cambodia_evisa_ports.value: Crossing from Vietnam into Cambodia on a Cambodian e-visa works only at Bavet (the Moc Bai road crossing on the HCMC to Phnom Penh bus route). The other Vietnam-border checkpoints — Kaam Samnor (the Mekong river crossing from Chau Doc), Phnom Den, Prek Chak (to Kampot/Kep from Ha Tien), Trapeang Phlong, Trapeang Sre, O Yadav and Banteay Chakrei — do not accept e-visa entry, though any of them can be used to exit. For those crossings a visa on arrival or an embassy visa is needed; check the current fee on evisa.gov.kh.
cambodia_evisa_ports.scope: Travellers entering Cambodia overland from Vietnam
cambodia_evisa_ports.support: Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation border-crossing table (hosted on the Royal Embassy of Cambodia in Berlin site, © 2026 MFAIC), read 2026-10-17: Cambodia–Vietnam checkpoints — Bavet (Svay Rieng) e-Visa entry Yes / exit Yes; Kaam Samnor, Phnom Den, Trapeang Phlong, Trapeang Sre, Oyadav, Prek Chak, Banteay Chakrei all entry No / exit Yes; 'you may exit Cambodia through any official exit point, regardless of your visa type'. E-visa fee not printed: secondary reports conflict (USD 30 all-in vs 30 + 6).

laos_evisa_ports.value: The Lao e-visa cannot be used at any Vietnam–Laos land border. Its accepted entry points are Vientiane, Luang Prabang and Pakse airports, the Lao–Thai Friendship Bridges I, II and IV, the Boten checkpoint and railway station on the China border, and Khamsavath railway station. Anyone crossing overland from Vietnam needs a visa on arrival or an embassy visa instead; processing of the e-visa itself is about three working days.
laos_evisa_ports.scope: Travellers entering Laos overland from Vietnam
laos_evisa_ports.support: Lao Ministry of Foreign Affairs e-visa portal, Information page, read 2026-10-17: 'eVisa can be used to enter through these following designated ports: 1. Wattay International Airport ... 9. Khamsavath Railway Station' — nine ports, none on the Vietnam border; 'The processing time of the eVisa is usually 03 working days'. Lao visa-on-arrival rules at Vietnam border gates were not verified here.

alcohol.value: Per entry: 1.5 litres of alcohol at 20% ABV or above, or 2 litres under 20% ABV, or 3 litres of beer or other alcoholic drinks.
alcohol.scope: All travellers entering Vietnam, per passport, per entry
alcohol.support: Vietnam Customs Department, quoting Decree 134/2016/ND-CP Article 6 verbatim: '1.5 liters of alcohol of >=20% ABV or 2.0 liters of alcohol of <20% ABV or 3.0 liters of other alcoholic drinks or beer.' The three limits are alternatives, not cumulative.

alcohol_overflow.value: A single bottle that exceeds the limit by no more than one litre passes duty-free in its entirety; beyond one litre over, only the excess is dutiable.
alcohol_overflow.scope: All travellers entering Vietnam, per passport, per entry
alcohol_overflow.support: Decree 134/2016/ND-CP Article 6 via Vietnam Customs: 'If the traveler carries a bottle or can of alcohol whose volume exceeds the limit by not more than 01 liter, the whole bottle will be duty-free. If the volume exceeds the limit by more than 01 liter, the exceed amount shall be dutiable.'

tobacco.value: Per entry: 200 cigarettes, or 250 grams of shredded tobacco, or 20 cigars. These limits do not apply to anyone under 18.
tobacco.scope: All travellers entering Vietnam, per passport, per entry
tobacco.support: Decree 134/2016/ND-CP Article 6(b) via Vietnam Customs. The under-18 exclusion is stated on the Customs Department's entry-procedures guidance.

goods_value.value: Other goods are duty-free up to a total customs value of 10,000,000 VND per entry, on top of the alcohol, tobacco and personal-belongings allowances.
goods_value.scope: All travellers entering Vietnam, per passport, per entry
goods_value.support: Decree 134/2016/ND-CP Article 6(d) via Vietnam Customs: 'Other items ... whose total customs value does not exceed VND 10,000,000.' Express this in dong; the USD equivalent moves with the rate and must not be frozen.

traveller_chooses.value: If you are over the allowance, you choose which items count inside it and which are declared — the decision is the traveller's, not the officer's.
traveller_chooses.scope: All travellers entering Vietnam, per passport, per entry
traveller_chooses.support: Decree 134/2016/ND-CP Article 6 via Vietnam Customs: 'Where the aforementioned allowance is exceeded, the traveler may decide which items are within the allowance and which are not.'

prohibited_list.value: The list of goods banned from import changed on 5 September 2026: Decree 69/2018/ND-CP applied until that date and Decree 292/2026/ND-CP applies from it. Anything over the allowance must clear customs as imported goods.
prohibited_list.scope: All travellers entering Vietnam, per passport, per entry
prohibited_list.support: Vietnam Customs Department, 2026: 'The list of goods prohibited from import is stipulated in Decree No. 69/2018/ND-CP (effective until September 5, 2026) and Decree No. 292/2026/ND-CP (effective from September 5, 2026).' Also Customs Law Article 54(2): luggage exceeding duty-exempt quotas must go through customs formalities like imported goods.

banknotes.value: Twelve banknote denominations are legal tender: six polymer notes of 500,000, 200,000, 100,000, 50,000, 20,000 and 10,000 dong, and six older cotton-paper notes of 5,000, 2,000, 1,000, 500, 200 and 100 dong. Five coin denominations exist but are rarely seen. The 500,000 and 20,000 polymer notes are both blue-toned and are the classic mix-up; the 100,000 and 10,000 are both greenish. There is no 1,000,000 dong note, whatever a scammer tells you.
banknotes.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
banknotes.support: State Bank of Vietnam, Money Issuance page, read 2026-10-17: polymer notes 500,000 (issued 17/12/2003), 200,000 (30/8/2006), 100,000 (1/9/2004), 50,000 (17/12/2003), 20,000 (17/5/2006), 10,000 (2006); cotton-paper notes 5,000, 2,000, 1,000, 500, 200, 100; coins 5,000, 2,000, 1,000, 500, 200. Tuoi Tre News, 24 Jan 2026, reporting the SBV's 23 Jan 2026 statement: 12 note denominations and five coin denominations all legal tender; 'the SBV also reiterated that it has no plan to issue a VND1 million banknote'. Colour-confusion note is editorial, not from the source.

legal_tender_dong_only.value: Inside Vietnam, payments, price lists, quotes and advertising must be in Vietnamese dong; pricing or settling in US dollars is restricted by law except in listed cases such as duty-free shops, services inside the isolated zones of international airports and border gates, fees charged by state agencies at border gates, and foreign-language promotional listings by airlines, hotels and tour businesses that still show the dong price. A business that insists on dollars is the exception, not the rule, and you can always pay in dong.
legal_tender_dong_only.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
legal_tender_dong_only.support: State Bank of Vietnam Circular 32/2013/TT-NHNN (effective 10 Feb 2014), implementing Article 22 of the Ordinance on Foreign Exchange as amended 2013. Article 3: in Vietnamese territory, except the Article 4 cases, 'all transactions, payments, listings, advertisements, price quotations, setting and writing of prices' may not be in foreign exchange. Article 4 exceptions read: clause 1 state agencies at border gates; clause 9 duty-free shops; clause 10 services in isolation areas at international border gates and bonded warehouses; clause 13 air transport, hotel and tourism businesses may list dong prices with foreign-currency equivalents on foreign-language websites and publications, menus and service price lists excluded; clause 16(b) residents selling to non-residents may quote and receive foreign currency. Guidebooks from 2015–16 saying USD is 'widely accepted' describe tolerated practice, not the law.

public_holidays.value: Vietnam's statutory public holidays total eleven days: New Year's Day (1 Jan), Lunar New Year (five days), Hung Kings' Commemoration Day (10th day of the 3rd lunar month), Victory Day (30 April), International Labour Day (1 May) and National Day (2 September plus one adjacent day). The Prime Minister fixes the exact Tet and National Day dates each year, and holidays falling on a weekend are taken on the next working day, which is why the real Tet break is usually seven to nine days.
public_holidays.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
public_holidays.support: Labor Code No. 45/2019/QH14 (English translation reproduced by Viet An Law), Article 112 clause 1: 'Gregorian Calendar New Year Holiday: 01 day', 'Lunar New Year Holidays: 05 days', 'Victory Day: 01 day (the 30th of April)', 'International Labor Day: 01 day (the 1st of May)', 'National Day: 02 days (the 2nd of September ... and the previous or next day)', 'Hung Kings Commemoration Day: 01 day (the 10th of the third month of the Lunar calendar)'; clause 3: 'The Prime Minister shall decide the specific public holidays' for Tet and National Day each year. Weekend substitution per Article 111(3) as summarised by lawnet.vn. The official English text on LuatVietnam is paywalled beyond Article 77, hence secondary.

tet_dates.scope: Lunar New Year's Day (first day of the first lunar month) in each year; Vietnam's Tet falls on the same day as the Chinese lunar new year except in rare timezone-edge years
tet_dates.support: Hong Kong Observatory Gregorian–Lunar calendar conversion tables (text format), read 2026-10-17: '2027/2/6 1st Lunar Month Saturday' (T2027e.txt); '2028/1/26 1st Lunar Month Wednesday' (T2028e.txt); '2029/2/13 1st Lunar Month Tuesday' (T2029e.txt). The 2027 date is confirmed by Vietnam's Ministry of Home Affairs holiday notice (see calendar.tet_2027_holiday). HKO computes for UTC+8; Vietnam uses UTC+7, which can shift the lunar date in rare years, none of which are 2027–2029.

tet_2027_holiday.value: The official Tet 2027 holiday for Vietnam's public sector runs seven consecutive days, Thursday 4 February to Wednesday 10 February 2027 (the 28th of the 12th lunar month to the 5th of the 1st), per the Ministry of Home Affairs notice of 9 October 2026. Expect government offices, banks and many businesses shut across that week, with transport at its most crowded in the days either side.
tet_2027_holiday.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
tet_2027_holiday.support: Ha Tinh provincial government portal, 9 Oct 2026, reproducing Ministry of Home Affairs Notice No. 11483/TB-BNV of 9 Oct 2026: 'ky nghi Tet Nguyen dan 2027 keo dai 7 ngay lien tuc, tu thu Nam (4/2/2027, tuc 28 thang Chap nam Binh Ngo) den het thu Tu (10/2/2027, tuc mung 5 thang Gieng nam Dinh Mui)'. Applies to cadres, civil servants and public employees; private employers follow the five statutory days plus weekend substitutions. The Ministry's own notice page was not opened.

medical_facilities_hanoi.value: A government-published list of medical facilities in Hanoi names, among others, Family Medical Practice Hanoi, International SOS Hanoi and Raffles Medical Clinic as English-speaking clinics with emergency medicine, Hanoi French Hospital and Vinmec Times City as English-capable private hospitals, and Bach Mai, Viet Duc and Army 108 as major public hospitals with some English. The US Embassy's own doctors list page has been taken down; this UK list (2022) is the most recent government list found.
medical_facilities_hanoi.scope: English-speaking travellers needing medical care in Hanoi
medical_facilities_hanoi.support: UK FCDO 'List of medical facilities in Hanoi and northern provinces', last updated 24 June 2022, read 2026-10-17: 13 facilities including Family Medical Practice Hanoi (clinic, English yes, emergency medicine), International SOS Hanoi (clinic, English yes), Raffles Medical Clinic (clinic, English yes), Hanoi French Hospital (hospital, English yes), Vinmec Times City (hospital, some English), Bach Mai, Viet Duc, Army 108 (public). FCDO disclaimer: providers 'for information only', none 'endorsed or recommended'. No payment-terms statement on the page. The US Embassy URL vn.usembassy.gov/u-s-citizen-services/doctors/ returned 404 on 2026-10-17.
medical_facilities_hanoi.note: Payment-up-front practice and the HCMC/Da Nang lists remain unverified; see _open_questions.

ho_chi_minh_mausoleum_2026.value: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum closes for about two months every year for maintenance of the body and building. In 2026 the closure runs 4 September to 2 November, reopening 3 November 2026; in 2024 and 2025 it closed from early June to the end of July or mid-August. Anyone planning Hanoi around the mausoleum should check the current year's closure window, and remember it opens mornings only.
ho_chi_minh_mausoleum_2026.scope: Visitors to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, Hanoi
ho_chi_minh_mausoleum_2026.support: VietnamPlus (Vietnam News Agency), 3 Sep 2026, citing Official Dispatch 1909/CV-BTL of 23 Apr 2026 from the Mausoleum Command: 'tu bo dinh ky tu ngay 4/9/2026 den ngay 2/11/2026', reopening 'tu ngay 3/11/2026'. Prior closures: 10 Jun–12 Aug 2024 and 2 Jun–31 Jul 2025 (Bao Lao Cai / Bao Quoc Te). Regular hours (mornings, closed Monday and Friday) appear on thuvienphapluat.vn behind a bot wall and are not asserted beyond 'mornings only'. The official site bqllang.gov.vn did not resolve.

electricity.value: Vietnam's mains supply is 220–230 V at 50 Hz, with sockets that take flat two-pin (type A/B) and round two-pin (type C) plugs; most hotel sockets are the hybrid kind that accept both. A US traveller needs no plug adapter for flat two-pin devices but does need to confirm each device is dual-voltage (100–240 V), because 120 V-only appliances such as hair tools will burn out without a converter.
electricity.scope: All travellers to Vietnam regardless of nationality
electricity.support: WorldStandards plug/voltage by country table, last updated 7 September 2025, Vietnam row: plug types 'A / B / C', voltage '230 V', frequency '50 Hz'. The IEC retired its World Plugs guide in 2026, so no standards-body page exists; Vietnamese sources commonly state 220 V. The dual-voltage advice is editorial.

climate_normals_source.value: The authoritative Vietnamese source for station climate characteristics is the National Center for Hydro-Meteorological Forecasting (Trung tam Du bao khi tuong thuy van quoc gia), which publishes climate profiles for Hanoi, Son La, Thai Nguyen, Phu Lien (Hai Phong), Vinh, Nha Trang, Pleiku and Ho Chi Minh City plus monthly and seasonal outlooks. Our month-by-region tables (geo.ts) should be checked against these station profiles rather than guidebook charts.
climate_normals_source.scope: Editorial reference for the climate layer
climate_normals_source.support: nchmf.gov.vn, read 2026-10-17: footer 'Trung tam Du bao khi tuong thuy van quoc gia'; Climate (Khi hau) menu with monthly, seasonal and climate forecasts; 'Dac diem khi hau khu vuc' station pages for Ha Noi, Son La, Thai Nguyen, Phu Lien, Vinh, Nha Trang, Pleiku, TP Ho Chi Minh. The English sub-site path returned 404.

_open_questions._note: Items needing a human or a better source; max 5 by rule. Each stayed OUT of the fact layer.

items.q: Hospital payment up front / direct insurance billing
items.why: No government page states it. The US Embassy doctors page is gone (404) and the UK FCDO list is silent on payment. Guidebooks (DK p274, Moon p508) say cash or deposit first. Structural rule only until a clinic's own terms page is cited.

CDC's Vietnam page does not say 'do not drink tap water'; it gives general food-and-water guidance. Keep the long-standing editorial line (bottled or filtered, ice in reputable places fine) without a fact span.

items.q: Mobile carriers and tourist eSIM terms
items.why: No official Viettel/VinaPhone/MobiFone page was found; only resellers. Decree 163/2024 on subscriber identification (passport registration) was not read in full. No key.

The embassy site's location pages return 404 and the State Dept country page could not be fetched this session. The existing consular_access key stands; the address needs a fresh read before any article prints it.

items.q: Cambodia e-visa fee and bus 152/T2 at Tan Son Nhat
items.why: Fee reports conflict (USD 30 all-in vs 30+6); evisa.gov.kh renders as a JavaScript app with no readable text. Which public bus serves Terminal 2 after route 109 moved to T3 (Apr 2025) is unverified.
